title: Power Weapons & Ballistic Ricochet Targeting
content: Conventional gunpowder firearms upgraded with high-velocity barrels and copper-jacketed ammunition. When you equip a Ballistic Coprocessor in your hand cyberware slot along with a compatible muzzle brake, your Kiroshi optics project a red ricochet trajectory off walls and floors, multiplying critical damage against targets behind cover.

title: Tech Weapons — Electromagnetic Acceleration That Pierces Walls
content: Electromagnetic railgun platforms that replace traditional firing pins with high-output charge capacitors. Holding the trigger unleashes charged Bolt shots capable of punching straight through concrete walls, metal doors, and heavy armor. Paired with Ping or a Kiroshi scan to tag silhouettes behind cover, they are devastating.

title: Smart Weapons & the Smart Link Tactical Interface
content: Weapon systems from Kang Tao, Arasaka, and Tsunami that fire fin-stabilized micro-missiles capable of curving mid-air once targets lock inside your reticle. They strictly require a Smart Link hand cyberware implant (or our protocol's optical bridge), though Tyger Claws jamming tattoos can deflect their rounds.

title: Iconic Pistols & Revolvers: Malorian 3516, Dying Night, Kongou, and Crash
content: Standout sidearms include the automatic Dying Night handed over by Wilson in Megabuilding H10, Kongou from Yorinobu's penthouse, Maiko's sleek Death and Taxes, the double-burst Tech pistol Lizzie at Lizzie's Bar, River's heavy revolver Crash, Jackie's La Chingona Dorada, and Johnny's brutal Malorian Arms 3516 with its incendiary alt-fire.

title: Iconic SMGs, Rifles & Shotguns: Fenrir, Yinglong, Overwatch, and Guts
content: Top long guns across Night City include Fenrir (an electrical SMG from Northside that shorts out enemy implants), Yinglong (a Smart SMG triggering EMP blasts), Shingen Mark V (thermal bursts with multi-target lock inside the Arasaka warehouse), Overwatch (a unique suppressed Grad sniper rifle), 6th Street's toxic Divided We Stand, and Rebecca's beastly shotgun Guts.

title: Iconic Blades & Katanas: Satori, Byakko, Errata, and Scalpel
content: Deadly melee classics abound: Satori (tucked away on the Konpeki Plaza helipad, delivering a brutal Hemorrhage combo when paired with Saburo's Nehan dagger), Scalpel (packing massive electrical crit bonuses during Sandevistan), Byakko (Wakako's reward with chained attack speed after every kill), and the thermal katana Errata hidden beneath the Santo Domingo power plant.

title: Cyberdecks — Camera Control & Offensive Netrunning
content: A netrunner's core operating system, replacing Sandevistan or Berserk to expand quickhack slots and max RAM. Tetratronic Rippler models supercharge damage during Overclock, Raven Microcyber accelerates Contagion spread, Arasaka decks favor covert netrunning, and the NetWatch Netdriver slashes RAM costs when hacking vehicles or cameras.

title: Sandevistan (Apogee, Falcon, Dynalar) — Extreme Neural Time Dilation
content: A spinal implant that overdrives the wearer's motor synapses, slowing perceived time around you by up to 85%. High-tier models like the Militech Falcon and Militech Apogee let you toggle time dilation on and off at will and refund duration with every kill—though they leave V without quickhacks.

title: Berserk (Biodyne / Militech) — Lethal Melee Invulnerability
content: An operating system built for aggressive melee fighters wielding hammers, bats, katanas, or Gorilla Arms. Once activated, it drains its temporary charge to prevent V's health from dropping below a critical floor while skyrocketing attack speed, restoring health on kills, and unlocking airborne ground-slam attacks.

title: Mantis Blades — Retractable Forearm Blades
content: Foldable blades concealed inside your forearms that launch a fast mid-range leap attack. They can be fitted with physical (bleed), thermal (burn), electrical (EMP), or toxic damage variants; with the Relic Jailbreak perk, they unlock devastating charged slashes after executing finishers.

title: Gorilla Arms, Monowire, and Projectile Launch System
content: Key tactical alternatives for your arm slots: Gorilla Arms grant up to a +6 passive bonus to Body checks for forcing doors and ripping off turrets while dominating boxing bouts; Monowire lashes multiple enemies at once and recovers RAM on hit; and the Projectile Launch System fires explosive or stun bursts straight from your wrist.

title: Leg Cyberware: Reinforced Tendons (Double Jump) & Fortified Ankles
content: Upgrading your legs completely transforms exploration and verticality across Night City: Reinforced Tendons enable a nimble mid-air double jump (pure gold when paired with Air Dash), Fortified Ankles deliver a higher charged super-jump with bonus armor, and Lynx Paws muffle your footsteps when moving in stealth.

title: Optical Camo, Second Heart, and Blood Pump
content: Top-tier defensive implants across the Integumentary and Circulatory systems: Optical Camo renders you nearly invisible for several seconds to break line of sight, the Biomonitor triggers automatic healing at critical health alongside the Blood Pump, and Second Heart immediately revives V upon hitting zero HP.

title: Stealth & Control Quickhacks: Ping, Memory Wipe, and Reboot Optics
content: In 2.x stealth netrunning, queue order is everything to keep enemy networks from tracing your position: uploading Memory Wipe first (Tier 4 eliminates trace buildup), followed by Reboot Optics and Sonic Shock, silently knocks out a target without triggering the hostile trace progress bar.

title: Combat Quickhacks & Elemental Combos (Short Circuit, Contagion, Synapse Burnout)
content: Exploit devastating quickhack synergies: Cyberware Malfunction stacks charges that amplify Short Circuit against mechs and bosses; Contagion followed by Overheat (or a thermal round) detonates explosive toxic clouds; and Synapse Burnout converts accumulated RAM spent during Overclock into lethal direct damage.

title: Ultimate Quickhacks & Vehicle Hacking in 2.x
content: Ultimate quickhacks (Cyberpsychosis, Suicide, Detonate Grenade, and System Collapse) carry steep RAM costs unless paired with Overclock and prior stealth takedowns. Since Update 2.0, netrunners can also remotely Take Control of enemy vehicles, slam their Emergency Brake during chases, or trigger Self-Destruct with a single click.

title: 2.x Attribute Trees: Body, Reflexes, Technical Ability, Cool, and Intelligence
content: The 2.x progression system lets you refund perks for free at any time (with one single-use Attribute reset per playthrough): Reflexes unlocks the essential Dash and Air Dash, Technical Ability expands cyberware capacity (via the Edgerunner perk) and Tech weapons, Intelligence unlocks Overclock, Cool boosts throwing knives, stealth, and revolvers, and Body anchors shotguns, LMGs, and health regeneration.

title: Cyberpsychosis: Empathy Loss, Dissociation, and Immunoblockers
content: In Night City, every implant erodes a person's sense of humanity and subjects the nervous system to chronic bioelectric stress. When combined with psychological trauma, poverty, or piling on military-grade chrome all at once, the mind fractures into paranoid violence against anyone nearby. Immunoblockers only slow the spiral temporarily—psychotherapy and scaling back chrome are the only real cure.

title: MaxDoc, Bounce Back, and Ripperdoc Cyberware Economy
content: In the current 2.x system, healing items (instant MaxDoc and regenerative Bounce Back) as well as grenades recharge on combat cooldowns rather than depleting finite consumables. Disassembling unwanted weapons instead of selling everything supplies vital Tier 1 through 5++ crafting components for upgrading your favorite chrome at a ripperdoc.

title: Legal Braindances (BDs) & the Lethal XBD Black Market
content: Technology originally developed in the 2000s for neurological therapy and repurposed into the 21st century's dominant entertainment medium: a recorder captures everything the actor experiences—sight, sound, heart rate, and dopamine spikes. In the illicit underground market, brutal real-crime XBDs thrive, edited and peddled by ruthless scavengers.

title: Rogue AIs, Sub-AIs, Soulkiller, and NetWatch Containment Protocols
content: Since the 2020s, three tiers of thinking software have existed: expert assistant algorithms (like my modified Zetatech base), lethal defensive ICE capable of frying human synapses (Hellhound, Kraken, Soulkiller), and truly transcendent rogue AIs born or mutated beyond the Blackwall after the DataKrash—utterly alien to human logic.

title: Night City Weapon Manufacturers: Budget Arms, Constitutional, Nokota, and Tsunami
content: Each manufacturer defines a clear social rung on the street: Budget Arms sells cheap disposable vending-machine pistols like the Slaught-O-Matic; Constitutional Arms builds Tactician shotguns and the fierce Unity pistol; Rostovic produces the wildest double-barreled shotguns; and Tsunami Defense Systems crafts elite precision rifles like the Rasetsu and Nekomata.

title: Iconic Cars & Bikes: Rayfield Caliburn, Quadra Type-66, and Kusanagi
content: Mechanical legends rule both the asphalt and the desert: the Rayfield Caliburn hypercar (with a free black unit stashed in Nash's Badlands cave), the classic Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech muscle car, the armored, weaponized Type-66 Javelina and Hoon for vehicular combat, and the blisteringly fast Yaiba Kusanagi CT-3X motorcycle.

title: Night City Streetslang (Choom, Gonk, Eddies, Preem, Chrome, Shard)
content: Essential streetslang: 'choom' or 'choomba' means a close friend; 'gonk' is an idiot or easy mark; 'preem' and 'nova' mean top-tier or awesome; 'eddies' are eurodollars; a 'shard' is a data chip; 'chrome' means cyberware; 'klep' means to steal; 'deets' means details or intel; and to 'flatline' means to die.

title: The Four Cultural Styles of 2077: Entropism, Kitsch, Neomilitarism, and Neokitsch
content: Night City dresses according to its tier of survival: Entropism grew out of functional poverty, repurposing scrap after the Time of the Red; Kitsch celebrates loud neon flair and style over substance; Neomilitarism enforces cold corporate tactical cuts from Arasaka and Militech; and Neokitsch fuses elitist opulence with limitless luxury materials.
